To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we propose a risk based optimization model for electric vehicle infrastructure response to cyber attacks.

we propose a mixed-integer linear programming model to minimize the security risk of malware spreading in the interdependent EV and power infrastructure while maintaining a satisfactory level of availability of EVSEs and power infrastructure components.

(1) The risk of cyber attacks in EV infrastructure is real and can propagate to other components of the smart grid, (2) The proposed response model is effective in reducing the risk of attack while maintaining a satisfactory level of service availability in the face of cyber attacks, and (3) The proposed response is more cost efficient than the traditional protection schemes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the risk based optimization of smart grid response in the face of cyber attacks to the electric vehicle charging infrastructure.

the following research questions: (i) How do attacks spread in the interdependent smart grid and EV infrastructure? (ii) How do we quantify the risk of attack spread and equipment availability? (iii) How can we optimize the risk of attack and equipment availability in a smart grid?
the security of the electric vehicle infrastructure in the context of cyber attacks.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the paper provides a mixed integer linear program (MILP) model to jointly optimize security risk and equipment reliability of the electric vehicle supply infrastructure in the face of malware attacks.
the proposed optimization model can be a valuable tool to help the grid operator and the EVSE provider to jointly optimize security risk and equipment reliability.
the proposed response model can provide a reasonable tradeoff between the risk of attack spreading to the smart grid and the equipment availability to supply the demand.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we provide a theoretical framework for the response of the power grid to the cyber attacks on the EV infrastructure.
a cyber-attack on the EV infrastructure is not only harmful to the EV users but can also spread to the power system.
a risk based response to attacks in the EV infrastructure is possible. However, the response is not without cost.
The main takeaway from our work is that
security risk and equipment availabilities are conflicting in nature and the proposed model provides a systematic way to balance these two conflicting objectives.
the response model can be used to provide the theoretical bounds for the tradeoff between risk of attack propagation and the level of equipment availability.
the risk of attack is not only related to the number of compromised EVSEs but also the location and connectivity of the compromised equipment.
